foil.title: Energy repricing risk from Black Sea maritime disruption state
foil.scenario_short: Black Sea maritime disruption, confirmed at 78% state confidence with 68% pressure, transmits through global crude spread stress to energy markets, keeping repricing risk elevated near 64% over 30 days.
foil.perspective_strategic: The 78% state confirmation and 68% pressure on global crude spread stress indicate a durable, not transient, disruption state; the single transmission edge to Energy suggests a focused market channel rather than diffuse risk, with 6 urgent critical signals reinforcing the energy repricing path.
foil.perspective_contrarian: The counter-evidence is the 75% confidence ceiling itself, which bounds action; the absence of directly matched Black Sea reporting—flagged as the key unknown—means the 78% state confirmation may be over-weighted relative to thin source diversity, allowing the contrarian branch's 56% projection to materialize if containment signals emerge.
foil.actor_lens: Commodity traders: Price whether stress in Black Sea becomes durable over the 30d. Rebalance positions if the probability path moves away from 64%.
foil.top_signal: Black Sea maritime disruption state is feeding energy repricing through global crude spread stress, with 68% pressure and 78% state confirmation

seismic-infrastructure.absence_reason: No product publishes a seismic forecast — earthquakes are not predictable, so there is no forecast/intel alternative to azimuth's observed USGS record. This is the honest inverse: for an observed natural-hazard fact, the sourced record IS the only trustworthy source.
